messages.subject: SE.type = fisher for large 3PL test
parts:
Hello, 

I am trying a few different methods for calculating standard errors on a "3PL" test with 63 items. When I use SE.type = "Fisher" I get the error "Error in rep.int(rep.int(seq_len(nx), rep.int(rep.fac, nx)), orep): invalid 'times' value). Here is an example: 

set.seed(2394)
a <- rep(seq(.75, 2.25, by = .25), 9)
b <- rep(seq(-2,2,by=.5),each = 7)
d <- b*1.072
guess <- rep(.1,63)

x<-simdata(a,d,3000,"3PL", guess = guess)
modelFisher <- mirt(data = x, 1, itemtype = "3PL", SE = TRUE, SE.type = 'Fisher')

When I try only a few items, everything works out well.
modelFisherLess <- mirt(data = x[,c(1,3,9,11,12,24,25,33,42,46,50,59,63), 1, itemtype = "3PL", SE = TRUE, SE.type = 'Fisher')  

When i try a few more items I get an error
modelFisherMore<-mirt(data = x[,c(1:3,9:12,24,25:33, 42:46, 50,59:63)], 1, itemtype = "3PL", SE = TRUE, SE.type = 'Fisher')
"Cannot allocate vector of size 28.0 Gb." 

This seems like a really large vector  - should I just use one of the other methods of estimation for the SEs? 

Thanks,
Briana

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: SE.type = fisher for large 3PL test
parts:
Hi Briana,

I wouldn't recommend using Fisher's information matrix in this case as it requires integrating across the possible response data space (which can be enormous, even for shorter tests). Methods based on the observed information matrix are likely better for IRT for this very reason, which is why the default is the numerical Oakes method. HTH.

Phil
